title: Android acquisition basics
quick: Android acquisition is the process of copying data from an Android phone. What you can reach depends on the lock state, encryption, the device model and what access is allowed.

sections.title: Starting points
text: First note the state of the phone: on or off, locked or unlocked, and the Android version. Isolate it from the network. Keep it powered. Then choose the least invasive method that works for that model.

sections.title: Common approaches
text: Many Android methods use Android Debug Bridge (ADB), a command line tool that talks to the phone over USB. It usually needs USB debugging turned on, which needs an unlocked phone. Other methods use a backup, an app that is installed temporarily, or manufacturer specific modes. Some need extra access to the system, such as root. Results vary a lot by model.
points: Manual review of the screen is the fallback.
Logical methods return data apps and the system agree to share.
Deeper methods need system access and can change the device.

sections.title: Encryption on Android
text: Most modern Android phones use file-based encryption. Files have separate keys. Some data is only available after the user unlocks the phone once since the last boot. This is why a restart can reduce what you can reach.

sections.title: Documentation
text: Record each command, setting change and tool version. Procedures and laws differ by country and agency, so follow your lab's own procedure.

example: A student practises on a spare test phone. They enable USB debugging, connect it to a computer, list the installed apps with ADB, and record each step. They then parse the result with a free tool and compare it with what the phone screen shows.
mistakes: Turning the phone off or restarting it and losing access to data.
Changing settings on the phone without logging it.
Assuming one tool works on every Android model.
Forgetting the SD card and the SIM card.
Running ADB commands without understanding what they change.

terms.meaning: Android Debug Bridge, a tool to communicate with an Android device from a computer.
An Android setting that allows ADB access.
Administrator level access to the Android system.
Encryption where each file can use a different key.

exam.q: Why should you keep an Android phone powered on and not restart it?
exam.a: After a restart some encrypted data stays locked until the user enters the credential again, so access may be lost.
It lets a computer send commands to an Android device over USB, for example to list apps or make a backup, if the device allows it.
